about: Every addition first-draft makes to a plain model call, with the paired, rendered comparison that justifies it. These entries are reviewed manually; npm test retains a real CLI integration for the multi-screen flow and its review. See CONTRIBUTING.md.
baseline: A plain call: one model call, the brief as the whole prompt, no system prompt of ours, no tools, the platform's own output limit, no style or direction.

verdicts.accepted: Repeated paired comparisons (same brief, same model) on at least two briefs, every one up, none down; or a delivery or policy reason.
verdicts.provisional: In the default make on a measured but mixed, bundled or missing comparison. Named with who decided it and the comparison still needed; review these entries manually.

entries.what: Polish this chosen design, not a new direction. Preserve its identity, palette, typography, composition, content, screens, ids and links except where the following feedback requires a targeted improvement. User feedback is cumulative and takes priority over judge suggestions; never undo an earlier request.
entries.reason: Owner-requested opt-in polish workflow, 29 October 2026: keep the selected direction and all user feedback across bounded rounds. This preservation policy does not change make, its initial scoring or its generation prompt; no isolated quality-gain claim is made. Independent visual assessments enforce promotion, not guaranteed fidelity.

entries.what: The pinned OpenDesign OD Next text-artifact recipe plus first-draft's static-host bridge, before the unchanged taste/page contract. The SHA-256 is the exact default-make prefix designPrompt() + two newlines + --- + two newlines + HOST_EXECUTION.
entries.note: Owner-requested engine replacement, measured as a bundle rather than isolated rules. Blind round one regressed (new 7/7.3 vs old 8/7.7). After the one allowed static-host integration repair, round two scored new 8/8, old 7.5/7 and plain 7/6.5. New also meets the original old scores 8/7.7. All scores remain below nine; no approved-layout match is claimed. Old/plain HTML was frozen, all frames freshly recaptured, and both rounds' blinding and failures retained.
entries.decided_by: Owner engine-swap brief, 2026-10-29: release only after overall non-regression on both required briefs
entries.needed: Repeated or isolated comparisons before attributing gains to any individual OpenDesign/static-host rule; this two-brief bundled result is not a variance estimate.

entries.what: A multi-screen flow brief keeps one shell and one grid on every screen (header with back and Skip, one title position, the progress dots, the round next button on every screen but the last, whose closing filled button is the only action), one idea and one decision per screen, each screen's own step label above the title, each screen fitting one screen (nothing runs past its bottom, so the dots and the next button stay visible and no option card is cut), and each screen's scene part of that screen's surface (full-bleed or a mask fade, no border, outline, frame, mat, drop shadow, oval or rounded clip, never a thumbnail).
entries.note: The flow gap the owner named from the mellow onboarding reference (25 Oct 2026): first-draft drew the screens but let each one invent its own layout, so the six never read as one flow. Stated in the contract; the critic also scores flow.shell and flow.character in its one review. Wording extended 2026-10-27 from the owner's six-screen review of the same flow: no rim on the scene, no thumbnail scene, each eyebrow its own step, one action per screen, and the closing filled button replaces the round next button on the last screen. `done` refuses a rimmed, inset or thumbnail scene on every flow screen, one step label repeated on every screen, two actions on the last screen, and a screen whose content runs it past the bottom of the screen it is shown on (src/render-check.mjs). No paired comparison yet.
entries.needed: A flow brief drawn with and without this sentence, both scored by a reviewer beside the same reference, on at least two flows.
